text:
maria: FYI I'm starting an RFC+implementation spike for OpenTelemetry SDK integration across our inference services (Python/Go/Rust). Main goals: low overhead, consistent span schema, safe defaults for hosted/dedicated/private. Thoughts?

sam: +1. We should standardize on OTLP -> collector for most deployments, with direct exporters only for special partners. Default should be batch async exporters.

jia: Agree. Couple quick constraints: 1) avoid creating per-token spans (too chatty), 2) provide hooks for detailed spans during debugging only, 3) make model_id/model_version first-class attributes.

kevin: For languages: Python's asyncio vs sync threads matters. Recommend using AsyncSpanProcessor in Python for our async inference workers and BatchSpanProcessor in Go. Rust (tracing) should use a compact exporter to avoid allocations.

maria: Notes from spike so far: we need these span attributes everywhere (string keys): model.id, model.version, route.policy, shard_id, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, gpu_id, quantization, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes. Also include inference.runtime_ms and queue_ms.

sam: +1 on attributes. Also add sampling.priority or error flag. For distributed traces across client->api->runtime->worker, use W3C traceparent propagation. Make sure our HTTP/gRPC gateways pass headers through without stripping.

jia: Quick example (Python) to propose as default bootstrap: 
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter

provider = TracerProvider()
otlp_exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="${OTEL_COLLECTOR}", insecure=False)
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(otlp_exporter))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
tracer = trace.get_tracer("redwood.inference")

# in async handler
with tracer.start_as_current_span("inference.request", attributes={"model.id": model_id}):
    # call into runtime, ensure we await properly
    ...
# explicit shutdown on exit: provider.shutdown()
```

maria: Good. Emphasize explicit shutdown in containers (preStop hook) to flush spans. For Python gunicorn/workers we need atexit + SIGTERM handler. Otherwise spans get dropped.

kevin: Go snippet for reference: 
```go
exp, _ := otlptracegrpc.New(ctx, otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint(os.Getenv("OTEL_COLLECTOR")), otlptracegrpc.WithTLSCredentials(creds))	pusher := sdktrace.NewBatchSpanProcessor(exp)
provider := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithSpanProcessor(pusher))
otel.SetTracerProvider(provider)
// defer provider.Shutdown(ctx)
```

jia: Rust (tracing) quick note: avoid heavy serde in hot path; attach minimal attributes and sample. Use collector with protobuf/compact encoding.

maria: Sampling strategy: parent_based(probabilistic) at SDK default + tail-based sampling at collector for error spikes. Default SDK rate maybe 1% for traces but always keep error traces. We'll need a config UI knob in Console.

sam: Important: for Hosted customers we can keep more traces for debugging but for Private/on-prem we must support air-gapped endpoints and mTLS. Exporter config should allow OTLP over gRPC with client certs.

kevin: Retention recommendation: raw spans for sampled traces: 7 days by default, errors and large regressions 30 days. Aggregated trace metrics (p95/p99, tokens per request) 90 days. Need infra to downsample.

maria: Privacy: DO NOT store prompt text. Instead store a hashed prompt_id + prompt_length. If higher fidelity is requested by customer, require opt-in and redaction review.

jia: Performance metrics: instrument an endpoint for microbench: measure p50/p95 extra latency from tracing enabled. Our goal: +<1% token latency with batching enabled. If >2% we disable detailed spans by default.

sam: Implementation checklist: 
- standard schema + attribute list (kevin)
- SDK bootstrap examples for py/go/rust (jia)
- Collector config + tail sampler + receiver auth (maria)
- Console UX for sampling/retention toggles per customer (product followup)

kevin: Also think about KV cache/span correlation. Cache hits should emit an event or span attribute (cache.hit=true) so we can correlate cost/latency differences.

maria: One tricky bit: continuous batching workers spawn many goroutines/tasks per request. We must ensure context propagation into kernel inference calls (C extensions). For Python C-extension runtime we may need to explicitly pass traceparent into C layer and rehydrate a span around kernel invocation.

sam: Good call. Also for quantized kernels we may want a lightweight metric rather than a span. Spans should be for user-visible boundaries.

otel-collector-bot: Reminder: OTLP data volume estimates: ~0.5-2KB per span avg. If we sample 1% across 100k req/day and 5 spans/req, that's ~5-10MB/day. Plan capacity accordingly.

maria: Action items: @jia will draft SDK snippets + unit test harness by EOD Fri. @kevin will publish attribute schema in GH. I'll draft collector config PR for default tail-sampler and mTLS. Ping me on infra channel if you want join spike. :rocket:

sam: Thanks — small follow-up: add a debug-mode that turns on per-token spans but gated behind env var and admin role. That will help repros without blowing prod.

maria: Yup. Also add rate-limits for debug spans in collector config so even if turned on we cap ingestion.

kevin: I'll add a small perf benchmark (python async path) and attach numbers to the RFC.

maria: Awesome, thanks all.
